transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it—after-hours intake is going to voicemail. What made you start looking to fix this right now?
User: We researched and found that answering these calls could significantly increase our client bookings and revenue.
Agent: Makes sense—those after-hours calls are often the easiest bookings to lose. After you close for the day, where do those intake calls go right now—straight to voicemail, or an answering service?
User: Right now, all our intake calls after hours go straight to voicemail.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly where bookings tend to slip away. Roughly how many after-hours intake calls hit voicemail in a typical week?
User: About 12 missed calls a week end up in voicemail.
Agent: Got it—about 12 a week going to voicemail after hours. What kind of business is this for (like HVAC, dental, law, something else)?
User: It's for a personal injury law firm.
Agent: Got it—a personal injury firm, and those after-hours calls are going straight to voicemail. When that happens, do you usually see those callers try again later, or do they end up going with another firm?
User: Most of them go with another firm if their call isn't answered immediately.
Agent: Yeah… that makes total sense in PI—people call the next firm fast. When they do get your voicemail, are you calling them back the same night, or is it usually the next day?
User: We usually call them back the next day, but by then, they often choose another firm.
Agent: I hear you—waiting until the next day is basically handing those cases to the next firm. Have you looked at any options yet to get those after-hours intakes answered live?
User: Yes, we've been researching options to have those calls answered live and increase our client intake.
Agent: Got it—so you’re actively comparing ways to get those answered live. Has anyone ever showed you the math on what those 12 missed after-hours calls a week could be worth in booked cases?
User: Yes, about 70% of them would book if someone answered. Average intake value is around $1,800.
Agent: Got it—so that’s about **$65,400/month** in intake value leaking just from after-hours missed calls. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—what’s better for you for that live call this week, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would be better for the live call. Could you please provide a specific time for the walkthrough?
Agent: Absolutely—before I lock a time in, quick check: **what time zone are you in—Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?**
User: We are in the Eastern time zone.
Agent: Perfect—Eastern time. What’s your first name?
User: I'm Marcus, from Bell & Associates Legal.
Agent: Got it, Marcus—thanks. And your last name?
User: My last name is Bell.
Agent: Thanks—Marcus Bell. And is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: No, the best contact number is +19172120001.
Agent: Perfect, Marcus—thanks. For **tomorrow (Thursday)**, I can do **11:00 AM** or **11:45 AM** Eastern—which works?
User: 11:00 AM Eastern works for me. Yes, book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Marcus—you're all set for **tomorrow at 11:00 AM Eastern** with Jay, and you’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if needed. Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, I'll wait for your confirmation.
Agent: Sounds good—keep an eye out for that SMS confirmation. Really glad you called, Marcus. Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great day—bye!
